title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 02
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'area calculation' function in a total station computes area by:
options: Coordinate method from surveyed boundary points
questions.solution: Total stations use the coordinate (shoelace) method to compute area from the N, E coordinates of boundary vertices.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In EDM, if the prism constant is not applied, the distance measured will have:
options: A constant systematic error equal to the prism constant
questions.solution: Omitting the prism constant introduces a constant additive error equal to the prism offset.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'surveying software' in a total station allows:
options: Storage, computation, and export of survey data
questions.solution: Built-in software handles data logging, coordinate computation, area/volume calculation, and export to external software.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'traverse computation' function in a total station:
options: Computes coordinates from measured angles and distances in the field
questions.solution: Traverse computation software calculates station coordinates from measured angles and distances using latitude/departure.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An electronic theodolite differs from a micro-optic theodolite in that:
options: It uses electronic/digital angle reading with display
questions.solution: Electronic theodolites use photoelectric angle encoders and digital displays instead of optical vernier reading.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'robotic total station' can:
options: Automatically track the prism and be controlled remotely
questions.solution: Robotic total stations have motorized drives and automatic target recognition (ATR) for one-person operation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'ATR' (Automatic Target Recognition) in robotic total stations uses:
options: Infrared or laser beam to detect and lock onto the prism
questions.solution: ATR uses an infrared/laser beam to automatically detect and align with the prism reflector.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The accuracy of trigonometric heighting with a total station depends primarily on:
options: The accuracy of the vertical angle and the distance measured
questions.solution: Trigonometric heighting accuracy is primarily governed by vertical angle accuracy and the horizontal distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'set out' (layout) function of a total station differs from survey mode because it:
options: Guides the user to predetermined design coordinates by displaying angle and distance offsets
questions.solution: Set-out mode computes the difference between current position and design coordinates, displaying the required angle and distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'polar layout' method in total station surveying sets out points by:
options: Measuring a horizontal angle and a distance from a known station
questions.solution: Polar layout sets out a point by turning a horizontal angle and measuring a distance from a known station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The primary purpose of levelling is to determine:
questions.solution: Levelling determines the difference in elevation (height) between points on the earth's surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A dumpy level has the telescope:
options: Free to rotate about the vertical axis
Fixed rigidly to the vertical spindle
questions.solution: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed to the vertical spindle and cannot be rotated in the horizontal plane independently.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A tilting level allows the telescope to be:
options: Tilted slightly in the vertical plane while keeping the bubble central
questions.solution: A tilting level allows fine adjustment of the line of sight by tilting the telescope without disturbing the bubble.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An automatic (auto) level uses:
options: An optical compensator to maintain the line of sight horizontal
questions.solution: An auto level has a compensator (prism system) that automatically maintains the line of sight horizontal after rough levelling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'line of collimation' of a level is:
options: The line joining the centre of the objective to the centre of the eyepiece
The horizontal line of sight through the centre of the crosshairs
The vertical axis of the instrument
questions.solution: The line of collimation is the horizontal line of sight passing through the crosshair intersection and the optical centre of the objective.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'back sight' (BS) in levelling is the first reading taken after setting up the level, taken to:
questions.solution: The BS is taken to a point of known elevation (benchmark or previous TP) to establish the height of instrument.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'fore sight' (FS) in levelling is the last reading taken before moving the level, taken to:
options: The same point as the BS
A new point whose elevation is to be determined
questions.solution: The FS is taken to a new point (turning point or change point) whose elevation is being determined.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'intermediate sight' (IS) in levelling is:
options: Any reading taken between the BS and FS at the same instrument setup
A reading to a benchmark only
The first reading after setting up
questions.solution: Intermediate sights are readings taken to intermediate points between BS and FS at a single instrument position.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the Height of Collimation (HOC) method, the reduced level (RL) of a point is calculated as:
questions.solution: RL = HOC - FS (or IS), where HOC = RL of BS point + BS reading.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The Height of Collimation (HOC) is calculated as:
options: RL of FS point + FS reading
RL of BS point + BS reading
RL of BS point - BS reading
questions.solution: HOC = RL of benchmark/back sight point + BS reading.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the Rise and Fall method, the difference between consecutive readings is calculated as:
questions.solution: Rise/Fall = Previous reading - Current reading. Positive = rise, negative = fall.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the previous staff reading is 2.350 m and the current reading is 1.850 m, the change in elevation is:
questions.solution: Rise = 2.350 - 1.850 = 0.500 m (positive indicates rise).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the BS reading is 1.500 m and the FS reading is 2.100 m, the difference in elevation is:
questions.solution: Fall = FS - BS = 2.100 - 1.500 = 0.600 m fall (FS > BS means the point is lower).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'turning point' (TP) in levelling is:
options: A point where both FS and subsequent BS are taken before moving the level
A point where the instrument is set up
questions.solution: A turning point is a stable point where both a FS (from previous setup) and a BS (from new setup) are taken.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'benchmark' (BM) is:
options: A permanent point of known elevation used as reference
questions.solution: A benchmark is a permanent point of known elevation established by previous surveys or government agencies.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The arithmetic check in the HOC method is:
options: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL
questions.solution: The check: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL (difference of RLs). If not equal, there is a computational error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The arithmetic check in the Rise and Fall method is:
options: ΣBS - ΣFS = ΣRise - ΣFall = Last RL - First RL
questions.solution: In Rise/Fall: ΣBS - ΣFS = ΣRise - ΣFall = Last RL - First RL. All three must be equal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Reciprocal levelling is used to eliminate:
options: Errors due to curvature of the earth and atmospheric refraction
questions.solution: Reciprocal levelling eliminates errors from earth curvature and refraction by taking readings from both ends.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In reciprocal levelling, the true difference in elevation between two points is:
options: The average of the two differences
The sum of the two differences
The larger of the two differences
(h₁ + h₂)/2 where h₁ and h₂ are the differences from each setup
questions.solution: True difference = (h₁ + h₂)/2, which eliminates curvature and refraction effects.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The curvature of the earth causes the staff reading to appear:
questions.solution: Earth curvature makes the line of sight (horizontal) pass above the curved earth, causing the staff reading to appear higher.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The correction for curvature per kilometre is approximately:
questions.solution: Curvature correction ≈ 0.0785 × D² km, where D is the distance in km.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Atmospheric refraction causes the line of sight to:
options: Travel in a perfectly straight line
questions.solution: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight slightly upward, partially counteracting earth curvature.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The combined curvature and refraction correction per kilometre is approximately:
questions.solution: Combined correction ≈ 0.0673 × D² km, which is about 7/8 of curvature alone (refraction cancels about 1/7 of curvature).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Trigonometric levelling determines elevation difference by:
options: Measuring the vertical angle and horizontal distance, then computing height difference
questions.solution: Trigonometric levelling uses H.D. × tan(α) (+ curvature and refraction correction) to find height difference.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In trigonometric levelling, the curvature and refraction correction is:
options: Always negative (subtracted from the computed height)
questions.solution: The combined curvature and refraction correction is subtracted because both effects make the target appear higher than it is.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'contour' is defined as a line joining points of:
questions.solution: A contour is an imaginary line on the ground joining points of equal elevation above a datum.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The contour interval is:
options: The total height of the area
The constant vertical distance between successive contours
questions.solution: Contour interval is the fixed vertical difference in elevation between two consecutive contour lines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Contours that are closely spaced indicate:
questions.solution: Closely spaced contours represent steep slopes; widely spaced contours represent gentle slopes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Contours that are widely spaced indicate:
questions.solution: Widely spaced contours indicate gentle slopes or nearly flat ground.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Concentric closed contours with decreasing values towards the centre indicate:
questions.solution: Closed contours with values decreasing inward represent a depression; values increasing inward represent a hill.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'contour interval' of 5 m means:
options: Every contour line differs from the next by 5 m in elevation
questions.solution: A 5 m contour interval means successive contour lines represent elevations 5 m apart vertically.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Contours never cross each other because:
options: A single point on the ground cannot have two different elevations
They are parallel to the ground
questions.solution: A point cannot have two elevations simultaneously, so contours never cross (except in rare overhang cases).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'depression contour' is shown on a map by:
questions.solution: Depression contours are shown with hachures (short ticks) pointing inward toward the lower elevation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'two-peg test' is used to:
options: Determine and adjust the collimation error of a level
questions.solution: The two-peg test checks and adjusts the line of collimation of a dumpy or tilting level.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the two-peg test, if the readings at A are 1.500 m (BS) and 1.700 m (FS), and at B are 2.300 m (BS) and 2.100 m (FS), the collimation error is:
questions.solution: True diff A-B from peg 1 = 1.500-1.700 = -0.200. From peg 2 = 2.300-2.100 = +0.200. Error per 2 m = 0.200; with equal distances, error is distributed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Cross-section levelling is performed to:
options: Determine the length of a road
Determine the ground profile perpendicular to a survey line or centre line
questions.solution: Cross-section levelling determines the transverse ground profile at regular intervals along a centre line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In profile levelling, the instrument is set up:
options: At intermediate positions along the centre line
questions.solution: The instrument is set up at intermediate positions to take BS, IS, and FS along the centre line and cross-sections.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'benchmark' used for temporary reference during construction is called a:
questions.solution: A TBM is a temporary benchmark of convenience established at a local point for short-term reference.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'benchmark' established by the Survey of India is called a:
questions.solution: GTS benchmarks are permanently established by the Survey of India with highly accurate elevations referred to Mean Sea Level.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Height of Instrument' method is also called:
questions.solution: The HI method is also known as the Height of Collimation (HOC) method.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The advantage of Rise and Fall method over HOC method is:
options: It provides an independent check at every reading
questions.solution: Rise/Fall provides a check at every staff reading (difference of consecutive readings), while HOC only checks at the end.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'change point' in levelling is another name for:
questions.solution: A change point (CP) is synonymous with a turning point (TP) — a point where both FS and BS are taken.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The line of collimation of a level should be parallel to the:
questions.solution: The line of collimation must be parallel to the bubble tube axis so that when the bubble is centred, the line of sight is horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the bubble tube axis is inclined by an angle α from the horizontal, the line of sight will be inclined by:
questions.solution: The line of sight tilts by the same angle α as the bubble tube axis, introducing an error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Curvature correction is always:
questions.solution: Curvature makes the staff reading appear too high, so the correction is subtracted from the reading (or equivalently added as a negative correction to RL).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Refraction correction is approximately:
questions.solution: Atmospheric refraction bends the视线 slightly upward, cancelling about 1/7 of the curvature effect.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In differential levelling, the error due to curvature and refraction can be eliminated by:
options: Keeping BS and FS distances equal (reciprocal levelling)
questions.solution: When BS and FS distances are equal, the curvature and refraction errors cancel out.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The purpose of levelling in mine surveying includes:
options: Determining the strike of coal seams only
Determining the gradient of haul roads and shafts
questions.solution: Levelling in mines determines shaft depths, haul road gradients, bench levels, and bench-to-bench elevations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'level line' is defined as:
options: A line parallel to the axis of the earth
A line lying on a level surface (equipotential surface)
questions.solution: A level line is a curved line lying on a level surface (equipotential surface of gravity).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'datum line' in levelling is:
options: An arbitrary or fixed reference surface from which elevations are measured
questions.solution: The datum is the reference surface (e.g., MSL) from which all elevations are measured.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Tachometry is a method of:
options: Rapid surveying using angular and stadia readings to determine horizontal distance and elevation
questions.solution: Tachometry is a rapid optical surveying method using a theodolite with stadia hairs to determine distances and elevations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The stadia hairs in a tacheometer are placed:
options: Equally spaced above and below the middle crosshair
At the top of the telescope
At the centre of the crosshair
questions.solution: Two additional horizontal crosshairs (stadia hairs) are placed symmetrically above and below the central crosshair.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'stadia interval' (s) is the difference between:
options: The upper and lower stadia readings on the staff
The instrument height and staff reading
questions.solution: Stadia interval (s) = Upper stadia reading - Lower stadia reading on the staff.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The horizontal distance in stadia tachometry is given by:
questions.solution: Horizontal distance D = Ks + C, where K is the stadia interval factor and C is the additive constant.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For a standard internal focusing telescope, the stadia interval factor (K) is:
questions.solution: For a standard tacheometer with internal focusing, K ≈ 100 and C ≈ 0.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The additive constant (C) for an internal focusing telescope is:
questions.solution: For internal focusing telescopes, the additive constant C is approximately zero.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the stadia readings are 1.200 m, 1.500 m, and 1.800 m, the stadia interval (s) is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: With K=100, C=0, and s=0.500 m, the horizontal distance is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In stadia tachometry, the vertical component is given by:
questions.solution: Vertical component = D × tan α, where α is the vertical angle of the line of sight.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the horizontal distance is 150 m and the vertical angle is +3°, the height difference is approximately:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The tangential method of tachometry uses:
options: Two staff readings at known vertical angles to compute distance
questions.solution: The tangential method uses two vertical angle readings (e.g., 15° and 30°) with staff readings to compute distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The subtense bar method measures distance by:
options: Measuring the horizontal angle subtended by a bar of known length at the instrument
questions.solution: A subtense bar of known length (usually 2 m) is subtended at the instrument, and the horizontal angle is measured to compute distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The subtense bar method is most accurate for distances up to approximately:
questions.solution: The subtense bar is most accurate for short distances up to about 200 m; accuracy decreases at longer distances.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In tachometric levelling, the reduced level of the staff station is calculated as:
questions.solution: RL = HI - VD - FS, where HI = RL of instrument station + IS, and VD = vertical component.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'tacheometer' differs from a standard theodolite by having:
options: Stadia hairs and a specially designed anallactic lens
questions.solution: A tacheometer has stadia hairs and an anallactic (stadia) lens to make C = 0 and K = 100.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'anallactic lens' (stadia lens) in a tacheometer is used to:
questions.solution: The anallactic lens is placed inside the telescope to make the additive constant C equal to zero.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'self-reducing tacheometer' automatically:
options: Replaces the need for a staff
Applies the reduction formulas to give horizontal distance and height difference directly
questions.solution: A self-reducing tacheometer has specially graduated stadia hairs that directly give reduced horizontal distance and height difference.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the stadia method, the horizontal distance formula D = KS + C assumes:
options: The line of sight is inclined
The line of sight is horizontal (for the basic formula)
questions.solution: The basic formula D = KS + C applies when the line of sight is horizontal. For inclined sights, modified formulas are used.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When the line of sight is inclined at angle α to the horizontal, the horizontal distance is:
questions.solution: For inclined sights, HD = KS cos²α + C cos α (approximate), where α is the vertical angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The height difference when the line of sight is inclined at angle α is approximately:
questions.solution: VD = (KS/2) sin 2α + C sin α for an inclined line of sight.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?
questions.solution: Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who founded the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution: Allan Octavian Hume founded the Indian National Congress in 1885.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Mughal emperor built the Red Fort in Delhi?
questions.solution: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in Delhi, completed in 1648.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Simon Commission visited India in which year?
questions.solution: Simon Commission visited India in 1928 to review constitutional reforms.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution: Indira Gandhi was the first woman PM of India (1966-1977, 1980-1984).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with which words?
options: B. We the people of India
questions.solution: The Preamble begins with 'We the people of India'.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with languages?
questions.solution: The Eighth Schedule lists recognized languages of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of how many members?
questions.solution: Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city?
questions.solution: Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, Punjab.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The chemical formula of common salt is:
questions.solution: Common salt is sodium chloride (NaCl).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which gas is used in the process of photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Plants use CO2 during photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The SI unit of force is:
questions.solution: Newton (N) is the SI unit of force.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which vitamin is produced when human skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.solution: Vitamin D is synthesized when skin is exposed to UV-B radiation from sunlight.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed on which celestial body?
questions.solution: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed on the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Missile Man of India'?
questions.solution: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam is known as the Missile Man of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: ISRO was established in which year?
questions.solution: ISRO was established on 15 August 1969.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Gaganyaan mission aims to:
options: B. Send Indian astronauts to space
questions.solution: Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme to send astronauts to low Earth orbit.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which of the following is the lightest metal?
questions.solution: Lithium is the lightest metal with a density of 0.534 g/cm³.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The pH value of pure water is:
questions.solution: Pure water has a pH of 7 (neutral).
